data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word leo, meaning lion. The name Leonilla conveys strength, courage, and nobility. In Christian tradition, it is also associated with Saint Leonilla, a Spanish martyr who endured persecution for her faith. The name Leonilla carries the meaning “Lion strength” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Leonilla usually hope their child will grow to embody lion strength and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Leonilla is of Latin origin, and its roots can be traced back to the Roman Empire where lions were symbols of power, strength, and courage. In various cultures, the lion has remained a powerful emblem of dominance and authority. The name Leonilla, therefore, carries these connotations and reflects the qualities of boldness, bravery, and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Susan or Leonilla (born 1300 in Segovia, Spain) is venerated as a martyr. She was arrested with a group of hermits and was subjected to intense physical and emotional torments in order to renounce her faith. Leonilla endured them all, refusing to compromise her love for Christ. Her unwavering determination and fortitude symbolize the triumph of the spirit and unyielding courage against adversity for many believers. In naming a child Leonilla, parents may be inspired by this saint's story and the deep spiritual values it represents, including unconditional faith, enduring strength, and unwavering courage.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Leonilla: Lioness of Christ. Embracing the strength and courage of a lioness, Leonilla embodies the fearless devotion to God. Her name inspires us to face challenges with grace and resilience, trusting in God's protective love.

historical_references.reference: A 16th-century Italian saint named Leonilla da Crissolo is venerated by the Catholic Church. She was born in the Lombardy region of Italy around 1522 and lived as a hermit in the wilderness near the town of Varallo. She was known for her austere lifestyle and deep spirituality. Leonilla died in 1560 and was canonized in 1607.

Another Leonilla, a Spanish nun and mystic, lived in the 17th century. She was born in Extremadura, Spain, and entered the Discalced Carmelite convent in Seville. Leonilla was known for her ecstatic visions and her profound understanding of the spiritual life. She died in 1651 and was beatified in 1734.
